title: Sharp Regime-Mean Sensitivity for Three-Stage Binary Treatment Regimes under Persistent Latent Coupling
banked_reason: D0.5.G tier=incremental < floor=field; paper_score_ceiling 5.3 < 7.4 and salvageable:false after math PASS.
gap_reasons: Because theta is completely unidentified from the factual law and the paper supplies neither an estimation problem nor a substantive application, the result functions as an exact diagnostic example rather than an identification result practitioners are likely to use broadly.

The closest accepted-bank partial-transport result (pid_slate_benefit_partialtransport_v1) is omitted from the positioning; directly distinguish its sharp transport/attainment kernel from this named-noise dynamic specialization before claiming theorem-level novelty.
proof_attempt_summary: Two proposal angles exhausted their revision paths; a third produced a mathematically sound sharp Cartesian regime-law projection, mean image, and simultaneous completions for a symmetric source-coupling family. The math panel passed, but D0.5 graded the delivered paper incremental below the field floor because the coupling is unidentified from the factual law and the example lacks an estimation or application case. The original adjacent-window and pairwise-independence comparison remains undelivered; a broader joint-source/channel extension would require a new reanchored proposal.
tldr: A three-stage binary regime benchmark holds its complete positive factual law fixed while coupling the early and terminal births with agreement probability \(\theta\). For every positive outcome-risk table \(q\), the exact conditional regime-law projection is the Cartesian box \(\prod_x[(1/4)\underline K_\theta(p_x,q_x),\ 3/4+(1/4)\overline K_\theta(p_x,q_x)]\), where the two transport costs have explicit likelihood-ratio allocation formulas and every point is attained simultaneously by one common-world terminal response. Its linear image is the sharp arbitrary-table regime-mean interval. The fair table \(q\equiv1/2\) yields the accessible sensitivity curve \([(16\max\{\theta,1-\theta\})^{-1},1-(16\max\{\theta,1-\theta\})^{-1}]\).
gap: Existing sensitivity analyses grade treatment ignorability or sequential confounding, local causal marginals diagnose lost global independence, and discrete causal programs provide numerical bounds; none gives the exact effect of a fixed cross-window birth coupling on a same-law three-stage regime mean.
fill: The project derives the exact coupling-indexed identified interval, proves source-faithful common-world attainment, anchors renewal and deterministic reuse as special cases, and isolates the nonfair simultaneous projection as the first-class open question.
